[49680 Value Chain Engineering Systems | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject equips you with the skills to optimise value chains, integrating engineering, IT, and management principles to enhance productivity, quality, and performance in various manufacturing industries. You'll learn to design value chain systems that comply with manufacturing practices and regulations, support growth, manage risks, and foster continuous learning. Through practical and theoretical approaches, you'll develop a comprehensive understanding of operations management, applying cross-disciplinary strategies to real-world challenges. This subject is ideal for production and operation engineers, supply chain enthusiasts, business analysts, consultants, and students interested in value chain systems within the manufacturing domain.

[49680 Value Chain Engineering Systems | Learning and teaching activities]
Teaching strategies for this subject include both ; (i) online learning activities including practice examples/problems, reading material and study notes and (ii) face-to-face in-class tutorials. The total allocated weekly hours for the activities are 3 hours.

Some class time will be dedicated to progressing group work and supporting students in the completion of the second assessment task. Students are encouraged to attend and actively participate in the in-class activities to improve their theoretical as well as practical understanding of the key concepts discussed in the class.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[49680 Value Chain Engineering Systems | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Identify key value chain drivers for Australian and global economies to provide clear pathways for continuous improvements in their teams. (B.1)
SLO2: Use operational and supply chain management tools to analyse distribution centres, transport, procurement and other components in the value chain. (D.1)
SLO3: Apply value chain tools to solve value chain problems and add value to an organisation. (C.1)

Professional standards
Engineers Australia Stage 1 Competencies

Students enrolled in the Master of Professional Engineering should note that this subject contributes to the development of the following Engineers Australia Stage 1 competencies:

- 1.5. Knowledge of engineering design practice and contextual factors impacting the engineering discipline.

- 1.6. Understanding of the scope, principles, norms, accountabilities and bounds of sustainable engineering practice in the specific discipline.

- 2.2. Fluent application of engineering techniques, tools and resources.

- 2.3. Application of systematic engineering synthesis and design processes.

- 3.4. Professional use and management of information.
